newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-ENQVIST ROLLS PAST RAOUX INTO INFINITI FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ENQVIST ROLLS PAST RAOUX INTO INFINITI FINAL.

text.p: Coming off a two-month injury layoff, Thomas Enqvist had few expectations of winning. Now nothing less than a title would satisfy the Swede.

Enqvist, the second seed at the $303,000 Infiniti Open, bounced Frenchman Guillaume Raoux 6-4 6-1 in 61 minutes Saturday to gain the final against the winner of the night match between top-seeded Goran Ivanisevic of Croatia and American Jim Courier, the sixth seed.
In early May, Enqvist tore two tendons in his left foot when he tripped over his equipment bag at a courtside practice session in Monte Carlo, and was sidelined until this week.
"I thought it would take more time to get into the matches," said the world's eighth-ranked player. "But you have more hat you want even more to win if you been away for a while."
Though surprised at how quickly he has returned to form, the 23-year-old Swedish Davis Cupper won't be satisifed with a runner-up trophy.
"It's a final," he said. "You go to a tournament to win. If I win I will be very happy and if I lose I will be very disappointed."
Enqvist will look to capture his second title of the year Sunday against Ivanisevic or Courier.

"Against both those players you have to be playing really well to have a chance to win," said Enqvist, who has an 11-1 lifetime record in finals. "That's the way it should be if you are in a final. A former number one and one of the best players in the world.
Enqvist showed world-class form to outclass Raoux, who had consecutive upsets over Australian Davis Cup stars Mark Philippousis and Patrick Rafter, seeds three and five.
"Thomas played much better than me today and there's nothing else I can say," said the 80th-ranked Raoux, who fell to 1-3 against the Swede.

"He's hitting first serve more than 120 miles per hour (193 kph) every time. He served maybe 60 percent of first serves. He never missed on backhand. He hit very well on forehand. He's moving very well. What else?
"He's doing everything better than me, so it's very difficult for me against those types of players who hit hard from the baseline."

"It's never easy," Enqvist said. "He's such a dangerous player that a couple of points here and there can turn the match around. But I think today I was the better player. I didn't make too many mistakes. I played steady, served well and returned well."
